title: Optimal Inference for Quantile Effects at Outcome Atoms under Mahalanobis Rerandomization
banked_reason: The proposed sharp globally capped two-axis Pareto surface is explicitly left open; the delivered LP characterization and scalar/collision envelopes are a weaker replacement.
gap_reasons: The proposed sharp globally capped two-axis Pareto surface (including least-favorable correlations and attaining rule) is explicitly left open; the delivered LP characterization and scalar/collision envelopes are a weaker replacement, so either resolve that object or retitle and reposition the contribution as the finite-envelope/LP result.

The advertised sharp off-collision frontier is not determined: the note proves only the nonmatching bracket f_{z_β}(ρ) ≤ liminf V_n ≤ limsup V_n ≤ U_β, and the same bracket for the tail-constrained value.
These envelopes neither assert convergence of either finite value nor identify either limit with V_β(ρ,ξ;R_ε).
proof_attempt_summary: The run derived an exact globally feasible tail-constrained finite LP, a two-sided half-sampling lattice/Gaussian comparison, bounded-chart transfer, fixed-interior singleton adaptation, and scalar lower/upper envelopes for the finite minimax values. The attempt to identify those values with one sharp two-axis Gaussian Pareto surface collapsed because the one-axis global comparison, same-kernel end compactification, sign-projection comparison, and uniform upper-epigraph transfer were not proved. Completing the promised kernel requires a new sharp-surface and global-transfer program; retitling around the LP/envelope result would be a separate topic rather than a repair.
tldr: For finite-population atom QTEs under balanced Mahalanobis rerandomization, the full observed-count problem admits an exact tail-constrained linear program and a computable optimizer. In the binary, two-stratum, one-balance setting, both the unrestricted finite value \(V_n\) and the exact tail-LP value \(\widetilde V_n\) have the transferred scalar lower envelope \(f_{z_\beta}(\rho)\) and universal collision upper envelope \(U_\beta\) for every fixed \(\rho>0\). The observable plug-in Gaussian statistic transfers coverage and diameter on bounded collision charts, and every tail-LP rule becomes a singleton exponentially fast at fixed interiors. The robust two-arm value \(V_\beta\) remains a Gaussian benchmark: no convergence to it and no optimizer equivalence between \(V_n\) and \(\widetilde V_n\) is asserted.
gap: Discrete-QE inversion is valid but not optimized for one atom QTE; regular rerandomization QTE theory does not resolve a fixed collision face; available experiment-comparison bounds omit half sampling with an acceptance shell. The corrected full count covariance and unequal-baseline action support are not handled by the prior draft.
fill: Characterize and certify the robust two-arm Gaussian Pareto surface, determine coupling sensitivity, prove strict comparison regions under exactly calibrated caps, and transfer matching procedures and lower bounds to the full accepted count experiment with an adaptive feasible rule.
